literal: Upon the lifetime of one who conducts himself having undertaken non-killing, Death who consumes life will not advance.
translation: Death, who devours lives, will not advance against the lifetime of one who adopts and practices non-killing.
modern: கொல்லாமையைத் தன் விரதமாக ஏற்றுக்கொண்டு வாழ்கின்றவனுடைய வாழ்நாளின் மேல், உயிரைக் குடிக்கின்ற எமனானவன் செல்ல மாட்டான்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme virtue of non-killing by stating that even Death, who normally devours all lives, will not cut short the life of one who practices non-killing. The word 'கூற்று' refers to Death, the divider of life, and 'உயிருண்ணும்' describes Death's nature as a consumer of life. By saying Death 'will not advance' (செல்லாது) against such a person's lifetime (வாழ்நாள்மேல்), the poet emphasizes that a life of harmlessness naturally commands longevity and protection from untimely demise.
